title: NSRTC 2026
subtitle: A three-day conclave on science, technology, and innovation
summary: Scientists, researchers, industry leaders, policymakers, innovators, and students met for three days of interdisciplinary discussion on emerging research and technology.
overview: The opening day examined the work recognised by the Nobel Prize and the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering. The inaugural programme included keynote addresses, awards for contributions to research and technological innovation, and a special lecture on generating national wealth through science and technology.

The following two days combined parallel technical sessions with round-table discussions, poster presentations, project exhibitions, and a Scholars-to-Scientists Connect initiative. Contributors came from universities, national laboratories, research institutes, industry, and public organisations.

title: NSRTC 2025
subtitle: Science, innovation, and national research priorities
summary: A three-day national meeting of scientists, technologists, policy leaders, and students organised around scientific achievement, cross-disciplinary research, and national research priorities.
overview: The opening programme considered Nobel Prize-recognised work in physiology or medicine, chemistry, physics, and engineering. Plenary speakers included Shekhar Mande, Vijayamohanan Pillai, Lakshmanan Muthusamy, and Deepak Ranade.

A formal inaugural ceremony brought together Vijay Bhatkar, N. Kalaiselvi, Ashutosh Sharma, Ashok Joshi, Prasad Khandekar, Milind Pande, and Vishwanath D. Karad. Kalaiselvi, Director General of CSIR, addressed students on pursuing excellence in professional work and in life.

tracks.name: Artificial Intelligence
tracks.summary: AI with cryptology, materials design, multilingual applications, responsible AI systems, digital twins, and AI in scientific discovery.

tracks.name: Advanced Materials and Processing
tracks.summary: Two-dimensional materials, CMOS and MEMS systems, clay-based electrolytes, carbon-dioxide conversion, and two-dimensional superconductors.

tracks.name: Digital Transformations in Energy and Sustainability
tracks.summary: Photonic circuits, quantum imaging, scalable energy solutions, fusion energy, and hydrogen syngas.

tracks.name: Healthcare, Pharmaceutical Science, and Biotechnology
tracks.summary: Infection control, nucleic-acid therapies, One Health, metabolic health, tuberculosis drug discovery, and plant-based bioactives.

programme.label: Day 1
programme.title: Plenaries and inauguration
programme.text: Plenary sessions examined Nobel Prize-recognised work across medicine, chemistry, physics, and engineering. The day continued with three special talks and the inaugural ceremony.

programme.label: Day 2
programme.title: Technical sessions
programme.text: Four parallel tracks covered artificial intelligence, advanced materials, energy and sustainability, and health and biotechnology. Round-table discussions and poster presentations connected young researchers with invited scientists.

programme.label: Day 3
programme.title: Advanced sessions and valedictory
programme.text: The four tracks continued with research on responsible AI, new materials, clean energy, metabolic health, and drug discovery. A valedictory session at Swami Vivekananda Auditorium included awards for outstanding poster presentations.
